svg.text: The image shop: from your laptop to a friend's laptop
Concept 11 · Practices 10–11 · GHCR = an image shop (registry) · by hand in Module 26, automatic in Module 29
the first package is always private
the official images from Docker Hub
(if the processor is the same; see below)
The author's lab: GHCR played by registry:3.1.2 on 127.0.0.1 (docker compose push 3.7 s, pulled again in a test folder); the login, the package page, and pulls from public GHCR not recorded.
A mold is made for one processor type
your own image follows the architecture of the machine that built it
the author's lab: a Pi 5 with Ubuntu
check an image: docker image inspect --format '{{.Os}}/{{.Architecture}}'
the official images (TimescaleDB, Grafana, Mosquitto, Caddy)
already carry many architectures: safe anywhere
An image built on a Pi or a Mac (arm64), pulled by a friend's Intel laptop (amd64):
Error response from daemon: no matching manifest for linux/amd64 in
the manifest list entries: no match for platform in manifest: not found
the friend's laptop builds them itself: docker compose up -d --build
(takes time and npm downloads; not tested by the author on amd64)
one image for both architectures at once = Module 29 (GitHub Actions)
the author's lab: the error above recorded against the stand-in registry, image linux/arm64
image: + build: in the same service
Compose PULLS first. An image not in the shop (not found):
a warning, then Compose builds it itself from the Dockerfile
(proven in the lab). That's why IMAGE_REGISTRY is required,
with no default: Compose won't pull someone else's same-named image.

text.tspan: … required variable IMAGE_REGISTRY is missing a value

svg.text: → the IMAGE_REGISTRY line in .env isn't filled in

text.tspan: invalid reference format: … must be lowercase

svg.text: → the account name in ghcr.io/… must be lowercase
